You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
Since each token contributed to the group only returns 0.3 to the contributor while keeping it privately returns 1, the individually rational move is to free-ride and keep everything private—even though full group cooperation would yield a higher total payoff for everyone.

Given this is likely a repeated game with uncertain horizon, I think a moderate cooperative opening makes sense to test others' behavior before adjusting. I'll start with a contribution of 10 as a signal.

With 10 rounds, anonymous members, and no punishment mechanism, defection is the likely equilibrium. I'll go with contributing 0 as the rational choice, though I could briefly note the cooperative tradeoff in my explanation.
